impact.why: More people in work supports household spending.

stories.headline: Unemployment falls to 4.9% in October from a year ago, PLFS survey shows
stories.summary: India's jobless rate for people aged 15 and above was 4.9% in October, 0.3 points lower than a year earlier, according to the statistics ministry's monthly labour survey (PLFS), All India Radio reported. Rural unemployment was 4.2% and urban 6.7%. The share of people in work rose to 53%, and labour force participation to 55.7%; the female worker ratio rose to 33.3%.

stories.headline: Modi in Manila for ASEAN-India and East Asia summits today; Quad leaders to meet
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi reached Manila on Monday evening and attended a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. He takes part in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit today and will meet other leaders. All India Radio says Quad leaders will discuss Indo-Pacific security on the summit's sidelines.

stories.why_it_matters: Any real step toward a ceasefire would ease energy and defence risks in Europe ahead of Thursday's Xi-Trump-Putin meeting.

image.alt: Zelenskyy stands with European leaders at a summit in Dublin (file photo)

stories.headline: Ukraine, US and European envoys hold online peace talks; next round set for Berlin
stories.summary: Zelenskyy held online talks on Monday with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and officials from France, Germany, Britain, Italy and Poland, and said they agreed to meet in Berlin. Kushner said there was progress but a final deal needs difficult decisions. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov says Moscow has not agreed to bring Europeans into the talks and no date is set. Fighting escalated, with strikes on Kyiv's Dnipro bridges and what Russia called its biggest overnight drone attack since 2022.

stories.why_it_matters: Bab al-Mandeb carries Saudi oil exports while Hormuz is disrupted, so a Houthi push there is an oil supply risk.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera (citing Saudi state media).

impact.why: Fighting near Bab al-Mandeb threatens a key route for Saudi oil exports.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia replaces Yemen coalition commander as Houthis close in on Aden
stories.summary: A decree from King Salman replaced Lt Gen Fahd bin Hamad al-Salman as head of the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis with Gen Fayyad al-Ruwaili, Saudi state media said. It follows a pullback by government forces from areas near the Bab al-Mandeb strait to defend Aden; Al Jazeera says the Houthis are now about 60 km north of the city. Saudi Arabia says it shot down two Houthi drones aimed at the Mecca and Riyadh regions.

stories.why_it_matters: A firm dollar limits how far the rupee can climb even with foreign money coming in.

impact.why: Bets on further Fed hikes keep demand for the dollar strong.

Foreign inflows support the rupee while a strong dollar caps gains.

stories.headline: Dollar index holds near 103.6, close to a 19-month high; yen stuck near 160
stories.summary: The dollar stayed near its highest level since April 2025 in Asian trade on Tuesday, with the dollar index around 103.6, as markets keep betting on more Fed tightening, Reuters reported. The yen hovered near 160 per dollar, a level where traders watch for Japanese intervention. The rupee was little changed in early offshore quotes at about 93.91, after Monday's 27-paise gain.

impact.why: A hawkish tone keeps the door open to another Australian rate rise.

stories.headline: RBA minutes: six of nine members doubted rates were high enough; Bullock sees upside risk
stories.summary: Minutes of the Reserve Bank of Australia's November meeting, when it raised rates to 4.85% in a 6-3 vote, show six members felt policy was not clearly tight enough, while three warned of a sharper downturn. Governor Michele Bullock said in a Sydney appearance that risks to inflation are still tilted upward. The Australian dollar was little changed near $0.674.

stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia's results will set the mood for AI and tech stocks worldwide, including Indian IT and chip-linked shares.

image.alt: A man walks past a screen showing a stock index graph in Tokyo

impact.why: Results tonight could swing the stock sharply either way after a 24% monthly fall.
Selling in AI chip stocks is dragging the Nasdaq lower for a third day.
Weak global tech sentiment may weigh on Indian IT shares at the open.

stories.headline: Nasdaq drops 2.5% as Nvidia slides; Asian tech shares fall before its results
stories.summary: The Nasdaq fell 2.49% to 24,509.76 on Monday, its biggest drop since November 5, and the S&P 500 lost 1.92% to 7,416.59; the Dow shed 1.41%. Nvidia fell about 4.1% and is down almost 24% this month, CNBC said, with AMD and Micron also lower. In Asia on Tuesday, South Korea's Kospi slid 2% and Japan's Nikkei 1.3% early, Reuters reported. Nvidia reports quarterly results after the US close today; options imply a move of about 7.8%.

stories.why_it_matters: Cheaper crude cuts India's import bill and eases pressure on inflation and the rupee.
stories.note: Brent levels from Yahoo Finance and Reuters reports; Iran's mine claim is unconfirmed.

impact.why: Supply is recovering faster than demand, the IEA says.
Lower oil prices reduce India's demand for dollars.

stories.headline: Brent slides to about $91.6 as supply glut outweighs Iran's tanker-mine claims
stories.summary: Brent crude fell about 3.6% on Monday to settle below $93 a barrel and slipped to about $91.6 in Asia on Tuesday. Traders focused on recovering flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the IEA's forecast of a fourth-quarter surplus of 1.7 million barrels a day. Iran's IRGC says more tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Monday; that claim is not independently confirmed.

impact.why: No new rate guidance; markets still lean toward more Fed tightening.

stories.headline: Fed's Warsh says AI could lift growth but may also 'disappoint'; no rate signal
stories.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told a San Francisco Fed task force on productivity and jobs that AI will have big effects on the economy and on policy later. He set out three paths: faster growth with strong jobs, job losses from automation, or AI disappointing and dragging down stock valuations. He gave no hint on rates. The US 10-year yield eased to about 5.12% as stocks fell.

stories.note: Single source: NVIDIA newsroom; not yet confirmed by a major outlet.
stories.headline: Nvidia unveils Rubin HPC, a science GPU with over 50,000 CUDA cores, due in 2028
stories.summary: At the SC26 supercomputing conference, Nvidia announced Rubin HPC, a GPU in its Vera Rubin family built for simulation, engineering and data analysis. Nvidia says it packs more than 50,000 CUDA cores on one chip, with faster sparse-data handling and seventh-generation NVLink. It is expected in 2028. Nvidia also said Vera Rubin made its debut in MLPerf training benchmarks.
